# Actual equal-critical cap charges retain height dipoles after global normal balance
terms when converting a boundary convex-order certificate to volume by
height weighting. It retains actual convex lattice-complete fibers, a
finite equal-critical cap cover, all proper central sections, section
centroid balance, and full joint concave-roof positivity for the selected
cover. The example is ABOVE the OC target and is not a bad minimizer.
A moving affine origin repairs this sheared-product calibration; the
calculation identifies what must be retained in a general argument.

## 1. Height Leibniz rule for the three-layer decomposition

In the notation of
`candidate d5b32c15d5673f71`,
fix one normal n and let h_p=x.n on its actual support face F_p.
Assume all heights are positive. For a used endpoint pair, write
h_-=y_-.n, h_+=y_+.n, h_0=(h_-+h_+)/2, and m=(y_-+y_+)/2.
The exact identity is

    h [delta_(0,m) - (delta_(-1,y_-)+delta_(1,y_+))/2]
      = h_0 [delta_(0,m) - (delta_(-1,y_-)+delta_(1,y_+))/2]
        + (h_+-h_-)/4 [delta_(-1,y_-)-delta_(1,y_+)].          (1)

The second term is an ORIENTED DIPOLE. It has zero total mass but
usually a nonzero affine first moment. Since h is constant on each
continuous face, multiplying the horizontal PSD term gives exactly

    h(-div_x div_x A)=-div_x div_x(h A).                       (2)

No continuous derivative of h appears along that face. Combining (1)
and (2) is the full height-weighted decomposition. Omitting the dipole
is an invalid product rule.

For a general anchored tuple with weights alpha_q and physical points
w_q=(q,y_q), mean w_0, and h_0=sum alpha_q h_q, the correction is

    R_h=sum_q alpha_q(h_0-h_q)delta_(w_q),
    integral w dR_h=-sum_q alpha_q(w_q-w_0)(h_q-h_0)
                   =-Cov_alpha(w,h).                          (3)

Its continuous-normal component is -Var_alpha(h), which is nonpositive;
other components need not have a scalar sign. In the binary case, if
D=w_+-w_-, the dipole is also the first divergence of

    [(h_+-h_-)/4] D integral_0^1 delta_(w_-+tD) dt.

That last representation passes through noninteger bases. It is a
signed-distribution identity, not an additional admissible mixed source.

## 2. Actual four-fiber model and finite common critical cover

Let

    P={0,p1,p2,p3},
    p1=(1,0), p2=(0,1), p3=(-1,-1),
    T=conv{(2,-1),(-1,2),(-1,-1)}, V=|T|=9/2.

The outer lattice triangle has exactly those four lattice points.
For example enumerate its integer bounding box [-1,1]^2 using
2z1-z2>=-1, 2z2-z1>=-1, and -z1-z2>=-1.
For 0<epsilon<1, use the lattice-preserving continuous shear

    b(z)=epsilon z1 e1,
    C_epsilon={(z,x+b(z)):z in conv(P), x in T}.                (4)

It is a full-dimensional convex body with exactly four positive integer
fibers K_p=T+b(p), all of area V.

Put

    ell_1=2z1-z2, ell_2=2z2-z1, ell_3=-z1-z2,
    u_1=(1,0), u_2=(0,1), u_3=(-1,-1).

Use the three actual caps

    H_i={10 ell_i(z)+u_i dot (x-b(z))>=0}.                     (5)

Each strictly captures its own outer fiber and strictly excludes the
two other outer fibers: ell_i(p_i)=2 and ell_i(p_j)=-1, whereas
-1<=u_i.x<=2 on T. It cuts a central triangle cap of area Gamma_2 V,
where Gamma_2=4/9. All three cap masses are therefore exactly

    Q=(1+Gamma_2)V=13V/9,    M=4V,
    beta=Q/M=13/36.                                           (6)

They cover the ENTIRE ambient space, because their three affine margins
sum to zero. Their positive continuous circuit has equal coarea weights:
each actual proper central section has coarea 2, section centroid zero,
and the three u_i sum to zero. There are no supporting-facet cap
coincidences. All outer traces are strict full or strict empty.

These are true GLOBAL critical caps, not merely equal numerical cuts.
At (0,0), its own triangle gives at least Gamma_2 V in every containing
halfspace. Couple the outer uniform triangles by cyclic barycentric
permutations: the three continuous vectors sum to zero, as do their bases
and their shear translations. At least one of the three coupled points
belongs to every closed halfspace through (0,0); integration gives outer
mass at least V. Thus the depth there is at least Q. The cover (5) gives
the matching upper bound. An exposed outer fiber has maximum depth
Gamma_2 V<Q, by isolating that fiber with a base tilt. Only the central
base is deepest.

This is the balanced selected cover from the archived simplex example
in `candidate ffc34ddb869ec7d5`, now
with a nontrivial explicit shear. Other critical covers make this family
nonminimal, as the archive proves; none of that is hidden here.

## 3. The actual Euler charge has all affine cancellations and roof positivity

Set W=(1/3)sum_i 1_(H_i), and let

    sigma=(W-beta) sum_p dS_(partial K_p).                     (7)

Retain the normal label when discussing a single facet. On each outer
fiber W=1/3 throughout its entire boundary, so its density in (7) is
-1/36. On a central edge, in its affine parameter t in [0,1],

    W-beta = -1/36 on the outer thirds,
               11/36 on the middle third.                     (8)

Let x(t) parametrize an original edge of length L. On that joint facet,
(7) has the exact positive-test decomposition

    sigma/L = w_triangle(t) delta_(0,x(t)) dt
       +(1/12)[delta_(0,x(t))
             -(1/3)sum_(j=1)^3 delta_(p_j,x(t)+b(p_j))]dt,     (9)

where w_triangle=-1/9 on the outer thirds and 2/9 on the middle third.
The first term is the ordinary triangle Green charge with its positive
kernel. The second is an ACTUAL three-input anchored Jensen term,
since the average of its three physical outer points is (0,x(t)).

Consequently every joint facet satisfies integral rho d sigma>=0 for
EVERY concave roof rho on its actual physical convex hull. Both signs
of affine rho are admissible, so sigma annihilates all affine physical
functions, separately at each normal. This verifies the required
critical affine cancellations directly, not just by a covariance test.

## 4. Positive height destroys those affine cancellations at one normal

The three original facets have unnormalized outward normals

    v1=(-1,0), v2=(0,-1), v3=(1,1),

support value one, and edge length L_f with L_f/|v_f|=3. At base p,
its FIXED-origin Euclidean height is

    h_(p,f)=[1+v_f dot b(p)]/|v_f|>0.                          (10)

Focus on f=3. The original charge has central mass L_3/12 and mass
-L_3/36 at each outer base. Multiplication by (10) gives total mass
zero but base first moment

    integral z h_(p,3) d sigma
      =-(epsilon/12)sum_j (p_j)_1 p_j
      =-(epsilon/12)(2,1) !=0.                                (11)

At epsilon=1/4 this is -(1/48)(2,1).

Thus, despite all the actual hypotheses above, the height-weighted
charge at this normal CANNOT itself be written solely as horizontal
PSD second divergence plus nonnegative anchored Jensen terms. Every
term of that proposed form annihilates affine functions, contradicting
(11). A constant shift of the origin does not repair (11), since it
subtracts a constant multiple of the original affine-annihilating
sigma. The missing correction is exactly the dipole in (3).

## 5. Global normal balance cancels first moments, not the dipole measure

Use the affine MOVING origin b(p), and write

    h_move=(x-b(p)).n,   h_fixed=x.n,
    D=(h_fixed-h_move) sigma,

now forgetting the normal label after summing all facets. The central
fiber contributes nothing. On an outer fiber W-beta=-1/36. Hence

    D=-(1/36)sum_j [b(p_j).n] dS_(partial K_(p_j))
      =(1/36) div_x [sum_j b(p_j) 1_(K_(p_j)) dx].              (12)

The sign follows from distributional divergence:
div(b 1_K)=-b.n dS_(partial K).

The vector facet-balance identity integral n dS=0 makes the total mass
and base first moments of D vanish. Its continuous first moment also
vanishes because sum_j b(p_j)=0. Nevertheless D is NOT the zero measure.
For the two genuine convex quadratic tests

    phi_+(z,x)=(z1+x1)^2,
    phi_-(z,x)=(z1-x1)^2,

the exact values are

    integral phi_+ dD = -V epsilon(1+epsilon)/9 <0,
    integral phi_- dD =  V epsilon(1-epsilon)/9 >0.             (13)

Indeed apply Gauss--Green in each translated fiber and use its centroid
b(p_j), together with sum_j (p_j)_1^2=2. For epsilon=1/4 and V=9/2,
the values are respectively -5/32 and 3/32.

Therefore the sum of the height dipoles has no fixed sign even on
convex quadratic tests. Genuine critical-normal balance, proper section
centroid balance, global affine cancellation, and positive heights do
not make that SUM vanish. The first-divergence/covariance term must be
retained rather than replaced by zero after checking its first moments.

## 6. Boundary-to-volume identity with every section term retained

For a fixed actual cap H={a.p+u.x>=c}, put t_p=c-a.p and use coarea
on its proper sections. For a smooth test phi and a chosen reference
c_p in the continuous fiber, Gauss--Green gives

    integral_(old boundary captured by H)
           phi (x-c_p).n dS
      = integral_(K_p intersect H) [d phi+(x-c_p).grad_x phi] dx
         +(t_p-u.c_p) integral_(section) phi dS/|u|.            (14)

This sign is checked by noting that the new cap face has outer normal
-u/|u|. Sum (14) with the actual critical weights, and subtract beta
times the full-fiber identity. The scalar volume terms cancel for
phi=1 because every cap has common mass Q=beta M; section terms remain
unless a separate actual balance eliminates them.

In the example (5), every proper section is at p=0 and u.x=0.
Both the fixed origin and the moving origin b(p) equal zero there.
Consequently ALL section-height terms in (14) vanish identically,
for EVERY test phi. At phi=1 both height-weighted scalar budgets are
exactly zero. Yet their difference is the nonzero signed D in (12)-(13).
Thus even complete disappearance of the section terms does not justify
dropping the bulk gradient/covariance term for nonconstant tests.

## 7. What an affine moving origin can and cannot do

The common affine origin b(z) removes the dipoles exactly in this
sheared-product example. That is the correct calibration, not a proof
that the height method fails universally.

For a general active binary support relation, a moving affine origin
c(z)=Bz+c0 removes its height dipole at normal n exactly when

    h_+(n)-h_-(n)=n.B(p_+-p_-).                                (15)

If that relation is active at every continuous normal, (15) for every n
means K_+ is a translate of K_-. This follows from uniqueness of a convex
body from its support function. Therefore a single affine origin cannot
flatten all active heights in a genuinely nontranslational family.
For example (1-a)K, K, (1+a)K at bases -1,0,1 have exact Minkowski
midpoint equality at EVERY normal, but for a>0 their support difference
2a h_K(n) is not a linear function of n for a full-dimensional compact K.
This last observation is a geometric obstruction to a universal gauge;
that auxiliary family is not asserted to furnish the critical cover (5).

The exact new requirement for a height route is therefore to pay or
cancel the remaining first-divergence terms using the actual joint cap
geometry. Neither their vanishing first moments nor the ordinary
simplex Green coefficient supplies such a payment. No below-OC
extremizer has been constructed or ruled out by these calculations.
